c0019.en: Designed by John Guerrero — chef and restaurant consultant since 2010, in professional kitchens since age 17 · johnguerrero.es

c0030.en: Clean uniform and work shoes, fresh apron, hair tied back and covered (cap or hairnet)

c0032.en: No hand/arm jewelry except a plain band; nails short, clean, no polish or acrylics

c0033.en: Cover cuts and wounds with a waterproof, brightly colored bandage and a glove on top

c0034.en: Wash hands at the handwashing sink on arrival and at every change of task: soap, hot water (at least 100 °F, FDA Food Code 5-202.12) and single-use paper towels

c0035.en: Check no one has vomiting, diarrhea, jaundice, sore throat with fever or an infected cut; if so, no food handling (FDA 2-201.11)

c0036.en: Turn on the exhaust hood and ventilate the kitchen BEFORE lighting anything else

c0079.en: Use the dropdown: ✓, — or N/A. N/A = not applicable, comes out of the total; — = not done, counts as pending.

c0431.en: Raw red meat and poultry, whole cuts

c0433.en: Portion BEFORE freezing: never thaw and refreeze

c0516.en: Write the report number of each inspection and the date of the next one in "Notes"

c0743.en: ▸ This is the checklist for the WHOLE RESTAURANT: what gets opened and closed for the entire building, not for each area. Use it as the backbone of the day.

c0745.en: ▸ Print the shift sheet (opening or closing) or use it on a tablet; the shift manager assigns tasks and each person initials theirs.

c0746.en: ▸ Each task comes with Assigned to and Due by preloaded with the kit's criteria: adjust them to your real schedule, they are green cells.

c0748.en: ▸ Everything filled in daily is GREEN: Assigned to, Due by, ✓ Done, Initials and Notes.

c0750.en: ▸ Mark ✓ in the "✓ Done" column (dropdown): that is the column that counts completed tasks.

c0751.en: ▸ "N/A" = not applicable at your restaurant: that task comes OUT of the total (don't delete it, mark it N/A). "—" = not done: it still counts as pending and lowers the percentage, which is the point.

c0752.en: ▸ The denominator counts the tasks written in the "Task" column, not a fixed number: if you add or delete tasks, the total adjusts by itself.

c0754.en: ▸ At the end of each table there are 5 free green rows INSIDE the range the counter covers: write your own tasks there.

c0755.en: ▸ If you need more, insert rows INSIDE the table (right-click → Insert), never below the last one: anything typed outside the range is not counted.

c0757.en: ▸ Sheets with formulas are protected WITHOUT a password: the input cells (the green ones) are unlocked, so calculations never get overwritten by accident.

c0758.en: ▸ You can insert and delete rows with protection on. To change the structure: Review → Unprotect Sheet.

c0762.en: ▸ Order of use: rounds → cash drawer. Each file covers one level: the rounds file marks the MILESTONE (turn on, open, close) and the cash file carries the MONEY. If a task shows up in both, it's on purpose: one is the milestone and the other the detail.

c0775.en: Turn on the main lights (interior and exterior)

c0777.en: Turn on HVAC / heat depending on the season

c0778.en: Raise security gate and open front door

c0779.en: Set up outdoor signage / menu board

c0781.en: Turn on the POS / card terminal

c0783.en: Turn on the reservation system / order tablet

c0785.en: Play background music at a suitable volume

c0786.en: Review today's reservations and special events

c0787.en: Check restrooms: paper, soap, cleanliness, air freshener

c0789.en: Check cleanliness of common areas (entrance, hallways)

c0794.en: Check that menus are in order

c0795.en: Turn on displays / info screens if any

c0824.en: ▸ The daily cash count: starting bank, drawer count by denomination, POS Z report and over/short — plus the monthly log to see at a glance which days didn't balance.

c0825.en: How to use — Cash Drawer Opening

c0826.en: ▸ Count the starting bank and type the amount in the GREEN cell "Starting bank (opening float)". The closing sheet reads it from there: no need to retype it.

c0827.en: How to use — Cash Drawer Closing

c0828.en: ▸ In "Cash Count by Denomination" fill in ONLY the "Quantity" column (number of bills or coins, whole number): the subtotal and TOTAL CASH calculate themselves. The table has US bills and coins (the penny is no longer minted but is still legal tender; a "25¢ roll" counts $10 and a "10¢ roll" $5). In the UK, Canada or Australia, unprotect the sheet (no password) and change the label and value of each row.

c0829.en: ▸ In the "Closing Summary" you only type three figures: "Card sales, excl. tips", "Other tenders + card tips paid in cash" and "POS Z report: sales + tax, excl. tips" (net sales plus sales tax, without tips or gratuities; many POS "total" lines include tips). Everything else is a formula.

c0830.en: ▸ The starting bank is deducted automatically: TOTAL COLLECTED = (cash counted − starting bank) + card sales + other.

c0831.en: ▸ OVER / SHORT = TOTAL COLLECTED − POS Z report (sales + tax, excl. tips). If the cell turns AMBER, the drawer doesn't balance: check it BEFORE signing.

c0832.en: ▸ One row per day: enter starting bank, sales by payment type, POS Z report and deposit; Total Collected and Over/Short calculate themselves and the over/short turns amber.

c0833.en: ▸ The starting bank is a balance, not a sale: the TOTALS row shows the AVERAGE starting bank of the days logged, not their sum.

c0834.en: ▸ Everything filled in daily is GREEN: Assigned to, Due by, ✓ Done, Initials, Notes, the count quantities and the summary amounts.

c0841.en: Write the starting bank in the green cell below

c0842.en: Check there is enough change (coins, small bills)

c0843.en: Check that the POS is on and open the register shift

c0844.en: Print the opening X report (start-of-day report)

c0848.en: Note issues from the previous shift

c0851.en: Deducted from cash on the "Cash Drawer Closing" sheet

c0854.en: Print the closing Z report (end-of-day report)

c0855.en: Cash count by denomination (see table below)

c0859.en: Total collected = (cash counted − starting bank) + card sales + other

c0860.en: Compare with the POS Z report → calculate the over/short

c0864.en: Prepare the bank deposit / put it in the safe

c0900.en: Enter how many bills, coins or rolls: a whole number (0 or more), no decimals.

c0913.en: "Cash Counted" is the drawer count AS IS, with the starting bank inside: Total Collected already deducts it. In TOTALS, "Starting Bank" is the AVERAGE starting bank of the days logged (a balance is not summed) and "Over/Short" is the CUMULATIVE over/short in absolute value: a +50 and a −50 make 100 of over/short, not 0. "Card Sales (no tips)" excludes tips; "Other + Tips Paid" = other tenders + card tips paid in cash from the drawer. "POS Z" = net sales + sales tax, without tips.
